keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «커피를 기르는 많은 농부가 아주 적은 돈을 번다(문제)» 와 «공정 무역이 답의 전부는 아니지만, 우리의 일상 선택이 먼 곳 사람들의 삶과 이어져 있음을 보여 준다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the problem (many coffee farmers earn very little) and the conclusion (fair trade is not the whole answer, but it shows our everyday choices are connected to people far away). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: Many coffee farmers earn very little when world prices fall

boxes.qen: How does fair trade help farmers?
boxes.a: A minimum price and an extra premium for their communities

boxes.qen: What are the limits of fair trade?
boxes.a: Certification costs money, and demand for certified coffee is limited

sumHowto.ko: 먼저 위 세 칸을 보고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 고르세요.
sumHowto.en: Look at the three boxes, then choose the right word for each blank.

sum.pre: Most coffee is grown by small
, and the price they receive can rise and fall sharply. Fair trade buyers agree to pay farmer groups at least a
price, plus an extra amount called a premium. However, certification costs
, and demand for certified coffee is limited. Even so, fair trade has made many
think about where their products come from. It shows that our everyday
are connected to the lives of people far away.

words: certification
인증
Under fair trade certification, buyers agree to pay farmer groups at least a minimum price
an official approval that something meets certain rules
premium
추가 금액, 프리미엄
They also pay an extra amount called a premium
an extra amount of money paid on top of the usual price
consumers
소비자들
our everyday choices as consumers are connected to the lives of people far away
people who buy and use products
harvest
수확물
farmers often sell only part of their harvest at fair trade prices
the crops that are gathered in one season
critics
비판하는 사람들
Some critics point out that certification costs money
people who point out problems with an idea
standards
기준
fair trade rules include standards against child labor and for environmental protection
rules that say how something should be done

qs.q: Why can some coffee farmers not even cover the cost of growing their beans?
qs.qko: 왜 어떤 커피 농부들은 원두를 기르는 비용조차 감당하지 못하나요?
opts: Because world coffee prices sometimes fall sharply
Because goats eat their coffee plants
Because fair trade does not let them sell
evs: When prices fall, some farmers cannot even cover the cost of growing their beans.
Most coffee is grown by small farmers in countries such as Ethiopia, Colombia, and Vietnam.
Whether or not that story is true, coffee is now one of the most popular drinks in the world, with billions of cups enjoyed every day.
Some coffee companies now also buy directly from farmers and share the details of their prices.
why: 본문에 가격이 떨어지면 어떤 농부들은 원두를 기르는 비용조차 감당하지 못한다고 나와요. 가격이 세계 시장에 따라 크게 오르내리기 때문이에요.
The text says that when prices fall, some farmers cannot even cover the cost of growing their beans.

qs.q: In the text, what does "address this problem" mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 «address this problem» 은 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: To deal with the problem and try to solve it
To write the problem on an envelope
To make the problem much bigger
evs: Fair trade was created to address this problem.
Under fair trade certification, buyers agree to pay farmer groups at least a minimum price, even when market prices drop.
Yet many of the farmers who grow coffee earn very little.
However, fair trade is not a perfect solution.
why: «address» 는 보통 «주소» 라는 뜻이지만, 여기서는 «문제를 다루어 해결하려 하다» 라는 뜻이에요. 바로 다음 문장에서 공정 무역이 최저 가격을 보장해 농부를 돕는다고 설명해요.
Here "address" means to deal with a problem. The next sentence shows how fair trade tries to solve it with a minimum price.

qs.q: Why might fair trade not help the poorest farmers very much?
qs.qko: 공정 무역이 가장 가난한 농부들에게 큰 도움이 되지 못할 수 있는 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: Certification costs money, and only part of the harvest sells at fair trade prices
Fair trade buyers pay less than the market price
Fair trade rules allow child labor
evs: Some critics point out that certification costs money, which the poorest farmers may not be able to afford.
Others note that farmers often sell only part of their harvest at fair trade prices, because demand for certified coffee is limited.
They also pay an extra amount called a premium, which communities can spend on schools, clean water, or better equipment.
Even so, fair trade has made many consumers think about where their products come from.
why: 인증에는 돈이 들어서 가장 가난한 농부는 감당하기 어렵고, 인증 커피를 찾는 수요가 한정되어 수확물의 일부만 공정 무역 가격으로 팔 수 있어요. 두 한계를 함께 봐야 해요.
Certification costs money the poorest farmers may not afford, and they often sell only part of their harvest at fair trade prices. You need both clues.

ends: How does a coffee bean travel from a farm to your cup?
커피콩은 농장에서 내 컵까지 어떻게 올까?
What other products can we buy as fair trade?
공정 무역으로 살 수 있는 다른 물건에는 무엇이 있을까?

write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «어떤 조건 + 그때 할 수 있는 일» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write your own condition and what we can do in English.
write.src: “If <u>we check where our products come from</u>, we can <u>support farmers who are paid fairly</u>.”

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «we can» 뒤에 «누구를 + 어떻게 도울 수 있는지» 를 써 보세요. (예: help children in coffee-growing towns go to school)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «we can», write who we can help and how. (e.g. help children in coffee-growing towns go to school)
